title: China tourist visa (L)
destination_description: Mainland China, for a holiday or a visit
visa_description: For tourism or visiting friends in mainland China. The consulate decides how long each stay can be.
source: China Online Visa Application (COVA) form and the Chinese Visa Application Service Center's L visa checklist

questions.prompt: What's the main purpose of your trip to China?
Will you work, study or do business in China?

stop_if.message: Work, study and business trips need a different Chinese visa (Z, X or M), which Ta'asheera can't prepare yet.

questions.prompt: How many times will you enter China on this visa?
questions.help: Most first-time tourists ask for a single entry.

questions.prompt: Let's add your passport. You can upload a photo of its details page and confirm what we read, or type the details yourself.
When was your passport issued?
questions.help: It's printed on the details page, usually next to the expiry date.

rules.message: The issue date can't be in the future.

questions.prompt: Where was your passport issued?
questions.help: The city or authority printed on the details page, for example Beirut.

questions.prompt: Which city or town were you born in?
And which country is that in?
What's your marital status?
What's your home address?
What phone number can the embassy reach you on?
questions.help: Include the country code, for example +961 71 123 456.

questions.prompt: What do you currently do?

options.label: I look after my home and family

questions.prompt: What's your job title?
questions.help: As your employer would write it, for example Accountant or Software engineer.

questions.prompt: What's the name and address of your employer or business?
Which school or university do you attend?
When do you plan to arrive in China?

rules.message: Your arrival date needs to be in the future.

questions.prompt: And when will you leave?

rules.message: You can't leave before you arrive.
Ask for up to 60 days per stay; the consulate decides the final length.
Your passport must be valid for your whole stay: a visa can't outlast it.

questions.prompt: Which city will you arrive in first?
questions.help: For example Beijing, Shanghai or Guangzhou.

questions.prompt: Which cities will you visit, in order?
questions.help: The consulate asks for a day-by-day itinerary; a short list is enough here.

questions.prompt: Where will you stay in China?
What's the name, address and phone number of the place you're staying?
Who's hosting you? Give their full name, address, phone number and how you know them.
Who's paying for the trip?
Who's your sponsor, and how are they related to you?
Who should be contacted in an emergency? Give their name, relationship and phone number.
Have you been to China before?
Have you ever been refused a Chinese visa or entry to China?

documents.label: Visa photo
documents.help: Colour, bareheaded, light background, 48 x 33 mm, taken in the last 6 months.

documents.label: Invitation or tour confirmation
documents.help: From a Chinese travel agency or the person you're visiting in China.

documents.label: Pre-paid hotel booking
documents.help: Hotel bookings for every night, paid in advance.

documents.label: Flight reservation
documents.help: A return booking showing your entry and exit dates.

documents.label: Day-by-day itinerary
documents.help: Where you'll be each day, with addresses.

documents.label: Letter from your employer
documents.help: On company letterhead: your role, salary, how long you've worked there and your approved leave.

documents.label: Business registration
documents.help: Your business registration and recent tax returns.

documents.label: Proof of enrolment
documents.help: A letter from your school or university confirming you're enrolled.

documents.label: Bank statements
documents.help: Your last 3 to 6 months of statements, showing you can pay for the trip.
